info: v6 -> v7 publication differences that are DECIDED to be acceptable, with the reason.
They are still compared and still REPORTED (verdict ACCEPTED, with the reason printed);
they simply do not count towards the exit code. Nothing here is silently normalised away.
Override the path with --accepted=<file>; pass --accepted=none to compare with no
acceptances at all (the strictest run, useful to re-check a decision).
Adding an entry is a DECISION, not a convenience: it says 'the published bytes differ and
the websites are still correct'. Record who decided it and why.

unordered_json_columns.indexation: Computed inverse index (component_relation_index / dd96). The set of entries must match exactly and is compared element by element; only the ORDER is ignored. v6 itself is not deterministic here - the column is calculated per publication from a PostgreSQL query with no total order, so v6 emits a different sequence on different runs. Decided 2026-08-12.

accepted_columns.restringidos.space: SCOPED TO THE rt1/restringidos COLUMN ONLY (node hierarchy72). v6 publishes a FABRICATED default map centre ({alt,lat,lon,zoom}) for records with no real geolocation; the v6 publication API strips it again before any website sees it. v7 publishes NULL there, which is the same information without the fiction. Decided 2026-08-12. NOT a blanket acceptance of every column named `space`: on games (node dd1269) v7 emits an OVERSIZED value where v6 emits nothing at all, which is an open defect, not an accepted difference.
accepted_columns.related: v6 writes '' where v7 writes NULL for a column it never populates. NULL is the correct v7 representation for an absent default and the publication API tolerates it. Decided 2026-08-12.

accepted_schema.reason: v6 tables carry an AUTO_INCREMENT surrogate `id`; v7 keys rows by (section_id, lang) directly. Part of the update, not visible to the publication API.
v7 promotes the natural key to the PRIMARY KEY instead of a secondary unique index. Same uniqueness guarantee, stricter declaration.
v7 widens the language column; every value that fit before still fits.
The v7 SQL generator does not render field_enum as a MySQL ENUM. The published VALUES are unchanged; only the column declaration differs.
